CHAPTER 8 — परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः (PARARTHE ATMOTSARGAH)

Introduction — आत्मोत्सर्गः किम्?

The title of this lesson joins two ideas. परार्थे means "for the sake of others" (पर = other + अर्थ = sake/purpose, locative अर्थे used adverbially). आत्मोत्सर्गः is formed by गुण-सन्धि from आत्मा + उत्सर्गः (आ + उ = ओ): the "offering up" (उत्सर्गः, from उद् + सृज् = to release, to give up) of one's own self (आत्मा). परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः therefore means the giving up of oneself — one's comfort, one's possessions, even one's body and life — for the good of others. Sanskrit tradition ranks acts of giving (दानम्) on a ladder: अन्नदानम् (gift of food) sustains for a day; विद्यादानम् (gift of knowledge) sustains for a lifetime; अभयदानम् (gift of fearlessness, i.e. protection) is higher still; but the supreme gift is आत्मदानम् or आत्मोत्सर्गः, in which the giver holds back nothing at all, not even the body. This senior-secondary lesson (NIOS Sanskrit, Course 309) teaches that ideal through the ancient, public-domain story of महर्षि दधीचि — the sage who donated his own bones so that the world could be saved — and through famous verses on त्याग (renunciation/sacrifice) and परोपकार (service to others). The Dadhichi legend is among the oldest in Indian literature: the vajra fashioned from the bones of दधीचि (दध्यङ्) is already alluded to in the ऋग्वेद (1.84), and the story is retold in the महाभारत and the पुराण literature.

कथा — महर्षिदधीचेः आत्मोत्सर्गः (retold in simple Sanskrit prose)

1. पुरा वृत्रः नाम महाबलः असुरः आसीत्। सः उग्रं तपः तप्त्वा वरं प्राप्तवान् — "शुष्केण वा आर्द्रेण वा, काष्ठेन वा पाषाणेन वा, लोहेन वा, केनापि सामान्येन शस्त्रेण मम वधः मा भवतु" इति। वरगर्वितः सः त्रीन् लोकान् अपीडयत्।
   Translation: Long ago there was a mighty asura named Vritra. Having performed fierce austerity he obtained a boon — "May my death come from no ordinary weapon, whether dry or wet, whether of wood, of stone, or of metal." Proud of that boon, he tormented the three worlds.

2. वृत्रः स्वर्गं जित्वा देवान् निरवासयत्। देवानां शस्त्राणि तस्य शरीरं स्प्रष्टुम् अपि न अशक्नुवन्। भीताः देवाः देवेन्द्रेण सह भगवन्तं विष्णुं शरणं गताः, "त्रायस्व नः त्रायस्व" इति च प्रार्थितवन्तः।
   Translation: Vritra conquered heaven and drove out the gods. The weapons of the gods could not even touch his body. The frightened gods, together with Indra the king of gods, went to Lord Vishnu for refuge and prayed, "Save us, save us!"

3. भगवान् अवदत् — "सामान्यैः शस्त्रैः वृत्रस्य वधः न शक्यः। नैमिषारण्ये दधीचिः नाम महर्षिः तपः चरति। तस्य अस्थीनि तपसा वज्रादपि दृढानि सन्ति। तैः अस्थिभिः निर्मितेन वज्रेण एव वृत्रः हन्तुं शक्यः। यूयं गत्वा तं महर्षिं याचध्वम्।"
   Translation: The Lord said — "Vritra cannot be slain by ordinary weapons. In the Naimisha forest a great sage named Dadhichi practises austerity. By the power of his tapas his bones have become firmer than even the thunderbolt. Only with a vajra fashioned from those bones can Vritra be killed. Go and beg that great sage."

4. ततः देवाः दधीचेः आश्रमं गताः। देवेन्द्रः सविनयं प्रणम्य अवदत् — "भगवन्! वृत्रस्य अत्याचारेण त्रयः लोकाः पीडिताः सन्ति। लोककल्याणाय वयं भवतः अस्थीनि याचामहे। एषा याचना कठोरा इति जानीमः, परं लोकरक्षायाः अन्यः उपायः नास्ति।"
   Translation: Then the gods went to Dadhichi's hermitage. Indra bowed humbly and said — "Revered one! The three worlds are tormented by Vritra's tyranny. For the welfare of the world we beg of you your bones. We know this request is cruel, but there is no other means of saving the world."

5. तत् श्रुत्वा महर्षिः ईषत् स्मित्वा अवदत् — "हे देवाः! इदं शरीरम् अनित्यम् अस्ति। परार्थे इदं शरीरं त्यक्तुं न कोऽपि शोकः। धन्यः अहम्, यत् मम अस्थिभिः लोकरक्षा भविष्यति। परोपकारात् परः धर्मः नास्ति।" इति उक्त्वा सः समाधिं गत्वा योगेन प्राणान् अत्यजत्।
   Translation: Hearing that, the great sage smiled gently and said — "O gods! This body is impermanent. To give up this body for the sake of others is no sorrow at all. Blessed am I, that by my bones the world will be protected. There is no dharma higher than doing good to others." So saying, he entered samadhi and gave up his life-breaths by yoga.

6. ततः विश्वकर्मा देवशिल्पी तस्य अस्थिभिः वज्रम् अनिर्मात्। तेन वज्रेण देवेन्द्रः वृत्रम् अहन्। पुनः त्रिषु लोकेषु शान्तिः अभवत्। अद्यापि दधीचेः नाम आत्मोत्सर्गस्य पर्यायः इव स्मर्यते।
   Translation: Then Vishvakarma, the architect of the gods, fashioned the vajra (thunderbolt) from his bones. With that vajra Indra slew Vritra. Peace returned to the three worlds. Even today the name of Dadhichi is remembered as a very synonym of self-sacrifice.

शब्दार्थ (Word meanings from the story)

असुरः = demon; तपः = austerity, penance; वरः = boon; शुष्कम् = dry; आर्द्रम् = wet; काष्ठम् = wood; पाषाणः = stone; लोहम् = metal, iron; शस्त्रम् = weapon; वधः = killing, slaying; अपीडयत् = tormented; निरवासयत् = drove out, exiled; शरणम् = refuge; त्रायस्व = save, protect (imperative); अस्थि / अस्थीनि = bone / bones; दृढम् = firm, hard; वज्रम् = thunderbolt; याचध्वम् = beg, ask (imperative, plural); आश्रमः = hermitage; सविनयम् = with humility; प्रणम्य = having bowed; अत्याचारः = tyranny, atrocity; लोककल्याणम् = welfare of the world; याचना = request, begging; उपायः = means, way; अनित्यम् = impermanent; त्यक्तुम् = to give up; शोकः = sorrow; धन्यः = blessed, fortunate; लोकरक्षा = protection of the world; समाधिः = deep meditative absorption; प्राणाः = life-breaths; अत्यजत् = gave up; देवशिल्पी = architect of the gods; अहन् = slew, killed; शान्तिः = peace; पर्यायः = synonym.

Moral of the story: The body is perishable; what endures is the good it does for others. Dadhichi did not merely give what he possessed — he gave what he was. His joyful, unhesitating gift teaches that परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः — self-sacrifice for the sake of others — is the crown of all virtues, and that true strength (the vajra itself!) is born of tapas and tyaga, not of metal.

सूक्तयः — Verses on त्याग and परोपकार (with अन्वय and meanings)

1) पिबन्ति नद्यः स्वयमेव नाम्भः स्वयं न खादन्ति फलानि वृक्षाः ।
   नादन्ति सस्यं खलु वारिवाहाः परोपकाराय सतां विभूतयः ॥
   अन्वयः: नद्यः स्वयम् एव अम्भः न पिबन्ति; वृक्षाः स्वयं फलानि न खादन्ति; वारिवाहाः खलु सस्यं न अदन्ति; सतां विभूतयः परोपकाराय (भवन्ति)।
   शब्दार्थ: पिबन्ति = drink; नद्यः = rivers; अम्भः = water; खादन्ति = eat; वारिवाहाः = clouds (water-carriers); सस्यम् = crop, grain; अदन्ति = eat; सताम् = of the good; विभूतयः = riches, powers.
   Translation: Rivers do not drink their own water; trees do not eat their own fruits; clouds do not eat the crops (they nourish); the riches of the good exist for the service of others.
   Moral: Nature itself is the first teacher of परोपकार; whatever the good possess, they hold in trust for others.

2) त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत् ।
   ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् ॥
   अन्वयः: कुलस्य अर्थे एकं त्यजेत्; ग्रामस्य अर्थे कुलं त्यजेत्; जनपदस्य अर्थे ग्रामं (त्यजेत्); आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत्।
   शब्दार्थ: त्यजेत् = one should give up; एकम् = one (individual); कुलम् = family; ग्रामः = village; जनपदः = country, region; आत्मार्थे = for the sake of the Self; पृथिवी = the earth.
   Translation: For the sake of the family one may give up an individual (interest); for the village, the family; for the country, the village; and for the sake of the Self (the highest truth) one may give up the whole earth.
   Moral: The verse teaches an ascending ladder of sacrifice — the smaller good must yield to the larger good, and the highest good of all is the Self/dharma.

3) अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् ।
   परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् ॥
   अन्वयः: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् (अस्ति) — परोपकारः पुण्याय (भवति), परपीडनं पापाय (भवति)।
   शब्दार्थ: अष्टादश = eighteen; वचनद्वयम् = two sayings; परोपकारः = doing good to others; पुण्याय = leads to merit (dative of purpose); पापाय = leads to sin; परपीडनम् = tormenting others.
   Translation: In all the eighteen Puranas, Vyasa has (in essence) but two sayings: helping others leads to merit; hurting others leads to sin.
   Moral: The whole of dharma condensed: serve, never harm.

4) वज्रादपि कठोराणि मृदूनि कुसुमादपि ।
   लोकोत्तराणां चेतांसि को हि विज्ञातुमर्हति ॥
   अन्वयः: लोकोत्तराणां चेतांसि वज्रात् अपि कठोराणि, कुसुमात् अपि मृदूनि (सन्ति); कः हि (तानि) विज्ञातुम् अर्हति?
   शब्दार्थ: वज्रात् अपि = than even the thunderbolt; कठोराणि = harder; मृदूनि = softer; कुसुमात् अपि = than even a flower; लोकोत्तराणाम् = of the extraordinary (beyond-the-world) persons; चेतांसि = hearts, minds; विज्ञातुम् = to understand; अर्हति = is able, deserves.
   Translation: Harder than the thunderbolt, yet softer than a flower — who indeed can fathom the hearts of the truly great?
   Moral: Dadhichi's heart was exactly such — flower-soft in compassion for the suffering worlds, vajra-hard in resolve when the moment of sacrifice came.

5) सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः ।
   सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग्भवेत् ॥
   अन्वयः: सर्वे सुखिनः भवन्तु; सर्वे निरामयाः सन्तु; सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु; कश्चित् दुःखभाक् मा भवेत्।
   शब्दार्थ: सर्वे = all; सुखिनः = happy; निरामयाः = free from disease; भद्राणि = auspicious things; पश्यन्तु = may (they) see; मा = not; कश्चित् = anyone; दुःखभाक् = a sharer of sorrow.
   Translation: May all be happy; may all be free from illness; may all see what is auspicious; may no one be a partaker of sorrow.
   Moral: The prayer of the Indian mind is never for oneself alone — it embraces सर्वे, all beings. This universal goodwill is the soil in which आत्मोत्सर्ग grows.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the lesson

(A) सन्धिः: आत्मा + उत्सर्गः → आत्मोत्सर्गः (आ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धिः); पर + उपकारः → परोपकारः (अ + उ = ओ, गुण); महा + ऋषिः → महर्षिः (आ + ऋ = अर्, गुण); देव + इन्द्रः → देवेन्द्रः (अ + इ = ए, गुण); न + अम्भः → नाम्भः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ); वज्रात् + अपि → वज्रादपि (त् → द्, जश्त्व-व्यञ्जनसन्धिः); कः + चित् → कश्चित् (विसर्ग-सन्धिः). Being able to split these (सन्धि-विच्छेदः) is essential for reading the verses.

(B) समासः: परोपकारः = परेषाम् उपकारः (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); लोककल्याणम् = लोकानां कल्याणम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); देवशिल्पी = देवानां शिल्पी (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः); महाबलः = महत् बलं यस्य सः (बहुव्रीहिः — 'whose strength is great', naming Vritra); वरगर्वितः = वरेण गर्वितः (तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः); दुःखभाक् = दुःखं भजते इति (उपपद-समासः).

(C) विभक्तिः: Purpose is shown by चतुर्थी (dative): परोपकाराय, पुण्याय, पापाय, लोककल्याणाय — 'for the sake of / leading to'. तृतीया (instrumental) shows means: अस्थिभिः 'with the bones', वज्रेण 'with the vajra', योगेन 'by yoga', तपसा 'by austerity'. षष्ठी (genitive) shows relation: दधीचेः अस्थीनि 'the bones of Dadhichi', वृत्रस्य वधः 'the slaying of Vritra', सतां विभूतयः 'the riches of the good'. सप्तमी (locative) appears adverbially in परार्थे, कुलस्यार्थे 'for the sake of...' and in अष्टादशपुराणेषु 'in the eighteen Puranas'.

(D) कृदन्ताः: क्त्वा-forms (having done X): तप्त्वा 'having performed austerity', जित्वा 'having conquered', श्रुत्वा 'having heard', स्मित्वा 'having smiled', उक्त्वा 'having spoken', गत्वा 'having gone'; ल्यप्-form: प्रणम्य 'having bowed' (प्र + णम् + ल्यप्). तुमुन्-forms (in order to X): हन्तुम् 'to kill', त्यक्तुम् 'to give up', स्प्रष्टुम् 'to touch', विज्ञातुम् 'to understand'. क्त-forms (past participles): निर्मितम् 'fashioned', पीडिताः 'tormented', गर्वितः 'proud'; क्तवतु: प्राप्तवान् 'obtained'.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः — the offering of oneself for the sake of others — is the supreme rung on the ladder of giving. You read, in simple Sanskrit prose, the ancient story of महर्षि दधीचि: the asura Vritra, protected by a boon against all ordinary weapons, tyrannised the three worlds; Vishnu revealed that only a vajra made from the tapas-hardened bones of Dadhichi could slay him; Indra humbly begged the sage, and Dadhichi, smiling, gave up his body by yoga, declaring that there is no dharma higher than परोपकार; Vishvakarma forged the vajra, Indra slew Vritra, and peace returned. Five verses deepened the theme — nature's selflessness (पिबन्ति नद्यः...), the ladder of sacrifice (त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे...), Vyasa's two-line essence of the Puranas (परोपकारः पुण्याय...), the vajra-hard yet flower-soft hearts of the great (वज्रादपि कठोराणि...), and the universal prayer (सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः...). From the text you drew grammar: गुण and other सन्धि (आत्मोत्सर्गः, महर्षिः, परोपकारः), तत्पुरुष and बहुव्रीहि समास, the dative of purpose (परोपकाराय), and कृदन्त forms in क्त्वा, ल्यप्, तुमुन् and क्त. Dadhichi's name remains, to this day, a synonym for the highest gift a human being can give.

topics.name: आत्मोत्सर्गः — The Ideal of Self-Sacrifice
topics.description: The meaning of परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः — the offering up of oneself for the sake of others; the ladder of giving from अन्नदान and विद्यादान up to the supreme आत्मदान; why Sanskrit tradition counts self-sacrifice as the crown of all virtues.

topics.name: महर्षि दधीचेः कथा — The Story of Dadhichi
topics.description: The ancient story of sage Dadhichi retold in simple Sanskrit prose: Vritra's boon and tyranny, the gods' appeal to Vishnu, Indra's humble request, Dadhichi's joyful gift of his bones, Vishvakarma's vajra and the slaying of Vritra.

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Senior-secondary Sanskrit vocabulary from the story and verses with English meanings: अस्थि, वज्रम्, शरणम्, अत्याचारः, अनित्यम्, समाधिः, वारिवाहः, विभूतिः, निरामयः, दुःखभाक् and more.

topics.name: त्याग-परोपकार-सूक्तयः — Verses on Sacrifice and Service
topics.description: Five famous public-domain verses on त्याग and परोपकार — पिबन्ति नद्यः, त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे, अष्टादशपुराणेषु (परोपकारः पुण्याय), वज्रादपि कठोराणि, सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः — each with अन्वय, word meanings and moral.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Sandhi, Samasa, Vibhakti and Krdanta
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the lesson: गुण, दीर्घ and व्यञ्जन सन्धि (आत्मोत्सर्गः, महर्षिः, वज्रादपि); तत्पुरुष, बहुव्रीहि and उपपद समास; the dative of purpose (परोपकाराय); कृदन्त forms in क्त्वा, ल्यप्, तुमुन् and क्त.

topics.name: Translation, Comprehension and Values
topics.description: Translating story passages and verses into English; comprehension of prose and verse; analysing the ethics of self-sacrifice and connecting Dadhichi's ideal to modern life — soldiers, organ donors, doctors and everyday service.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the meaning of परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः (self-sacrifice for the sake of others), derive the word आत्मोत्सर्गः, and describe the ladder of giving that places आत्मदान at the top.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: महर्षि दधीचेः कथा — The Story of Dadhichi
learning_outcomes.description: Recall the characters and sequence of events of the Dadhichi story — Vritra's boon, the gods' appeal, Vishnu's counsel, Dadhichi's gift, Vishvakarma's vajra and Vritra's slaying.
