chapter_summary.title: परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः (Pararthe Atmotsargah) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary for Chapter 8 presents the supreme ideal of self-sacrifice for others through the ancient story of महर्षि दधीचि, who gave his own bones for the vajra that slew Vritra. It also explains five famous verses on त्याग and परोपकार, and the grammar — सन्धि, समास, विभक्ति and कृदन्त — drawn from the text.

branches.label: अर्थः — Meaning of the ideal
details: परार्थे = for the sake of others
आत्मा + उत्सर्गः = offering up oneself (गुण-सन्धि)
Ladder of giving: अन्नदान → विद्यादान → अभयदान → आत्मदान
Self-sacrifice is the crown of all virtues

branches.label: कथा — Dadhichi's story
details: Vritra's boon: no ordinary weapon can kill him
Gods take refuge with Vishnu
Only a vajra from Dadhichi's bones can slay Vritra
Dadhichi gives up his body by yoga, smiling
Vishvakarma forges the vajra; Indra slays Vritra

branches.label: सूक्तयः — Key verses
details: पिबन्ति नद्यः... परोपकाराय सतां विभूतयः
त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे... आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत्
परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्
वज्रादपि कठोराणि मृदूनि कुसुमादपि
सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः...

branches.label: व्याकरणम् — Grammar
details: गुण-सन्धि: आत्मोत्सर्गः, परोपकारः, महर्षिः
समास: परोपकारः (ष.तत्पुरुष), महाबलः (बहुव्रीहि)
चतुर्थी of purpose: परोपकाराय, लोककल्याणाय
कृदन्त: उक्त्वा, प्रणम्य, हन्तुम्, निर्मितम्

branches.label: मूल्यानि — Values today
details: The smaller good yields to the larger good
True strength is born of tapas and tyaga
Modern Dadhichis: soldiers, organ donors, selfless doctors
Universal goodwill: may all be happy, none suffer

sections.heading: The ideal of self-sacrifice
bullets: परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः means the offering up (उत्सर्गः) of one's own self (आत्मा) for the sake of others (परार्थे); the compound आत्मोत्सर्गः is formed by गुण-सन्धि (आ + उ = ओ).

Sanskrit tradition ranks giving on a ladder — gift of food sustains for a day, gift of knowledge for a lifetime, gift of protection longer still — but the gift of oneself (आत्मदानम्) is supreme because nothing is held back.
The lesson's message: the body is perishable (अनित्यम्); what endures is the good done through it for others.

sections.heading: The story of Dadhichi and the vajra
bullets: The asura Vritra won a boon that no ordinary weapon — dry or wet, of wood, stone or metal — could kill him, and then tyrannised the three worlds and drove the gods from heaven.
Vishnu revealed that only a vajra fashioned from the tapas-hardened bones of sage Dadhichi could slay Vritra, so Indra went to the sage's hermitage and humbly begged for his bones for लोककल्याण.
Dadhichi smiled and said the impermanent body is no loss when given परार्थे — 'blessed am I that my bones will protect the world' — and gave up his life by yoga.
Vishvakarma forged the vajra from the bones, Indra slew Vritra, and peace returned; the legend is as old as the ऋग्वेद (1.84) and is retold in the Mahabharata and Puranas.
The vajra's real strength came not from metal but from a sage's tapas and tyaga — a symbol that character is the hardest substance in the world.

sections.heading: Verses on tyaga and paropakara
bullets: पिबन्ति नद्यः...: rivers, trees and clouds never consume what they carry — the riches of the good exist परोपकाराय, for others.
त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे...: an ascending ladder — give up the individual for the family, the family for the village, the village for the country, and everything for the highest Self.
अष्टादशपुराणेषु...: Vyasa's essence of all eighteen Puranas in two phrases — परोपकारः पुण्याय, पापाय परपीडनम् (service earns merit, harming others earns sin).
वज्रादपि कठोराणि मृदूनि कुसुमादपि: the hearts of the great are harder than the thunderbolt yet softer than a flower — exactly Dadhichi's heart.
सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः...: the universal prayer that all be happy, healthy and free of sorrow — the soil in which self-sacrifice grows.

sections.heading: Grammar from the lesson
bullets: गुण-सन्धि: आत्मा + उत्सर्गः = आत्मोत्सर्गः, पर + उपकारः = परोपकारः, महा + ऋषिः = महर्षिः, देव + इन्द्रः = देवेन्द्रः; दीर्घ: न + अम्भः = नाम्भः; व्यञ्जन (जश्त्व): वज्रात् + अपि = वज्रादपि.
समास: परोपकारः and लोककल्याणम् are षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष; महाबलः (महत् बलं यस्य सः) is बहुव्रीहि; वरगर्वितः is तृतीया-तत्पुरुष.
विभक्ति: चतुर्थी shows purpose (परोपकाराय, पुण्याय, लोककल्याणाय); तृतीया shows means (अस्थिभिः, वज्रेण, योगेन); षष्ठी shows relation (दधीचेः, वृत्रस्य, सताम्).
कृदन्त: क्त्वा — तप्त्वा, श्रुत्वा, उक्त्वा; ल्यप् — प्रणम्य; तुमुन् — हन्तुम्, त्यक्तुम्, विज्ञातुम्; क्त — निर्मितम्, पीडिताः; क्तवतु — प्राप्तवान्.

sections.heading: Values for today
bullets: The ladder of त्यजेदेकं teaches that in a clash of goods, the larger good has the higher claim — the principle behind civic duty and public service.
Modern Dadhichis surround us: soldiers who give their lives, organ and body donors, doctors and volunteers in epidemics, whistle-blowers who risk everything for the public good.
Not every sacrifice is of life — giving one's time, comfort, talent and resources for others is आत्मोत्सर्ग in daily practice.
The prayer सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः widens the heart from 'me and mine' to all beings — the attitude from which true sacrifice becomes possible.

key_takeaways: परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः — giving up oneself for the sake of others — is the supreme rung on the ladder of दान.
Dadhichi gave not what he possessed but what he was: his own bones became the vajra that saved the three worlds.
True strength is born of tapas and tyaga, not metal — the vajra was mightier than every weapon because it was made of a sage's sacrifice.
Nature teaches परोपकार: rivers, trees and clouds never consume what they carry (पिबन्ति नद्यः...).
Vyasa's essence of all the Puranas: परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् — serve others, never harm them.
The hearts of the great are वज्रादपि कठोराणि, कुसुमादपि मृदूनि — hard as the vajra in resolve, soft as a flower in compassion.
Grammar: आत्मोत्सर्गः, परोपकारः and महर्षिः are गुण-सन्धि forms; चतुर्थी (परोपकाराय) expresses purpose; क्त्वा/ल्यप्/तुमुन्/क्त are the key कृदन्त forms of the lesson.

glossary.definition: The offering up of oneself (आत्मा + उत्सर्गः, गुण-सन्धि); self-sacrifice, the supreme form of giving.
For the sake of others (पर + अर्थे); the adverbial locative that names the motive of true sacrifice.
Doing good to others (परेषाम् उपकारः, षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष); the virtue that Vyasa says leads to पुण्य.
The mighty asura who, protected by a boon against ordinary weapons, tyrannised the three worlds until slain by Indra's vajra.
The great sage (महर्षि) of the Naimisha forest who joyfully gave his bones for the vajra; a byword for self-sacrifice.
The thunderbolt weapon of Indra, fashioned by Vishvakarma from Dadhichi's tapas-hardened bones.
Bone; plural अस्थीनि — the bones of Dadhichi from which the vajra was made.
The architect and craftsman of the gods (देवशिल्पी), who forged the vajra from the sage's bones.
Austerity, penance; the inner discipline whose power made Dadhichi's bones firmer than the thunderbolt.
The gift of fearlessness — giving protection to a frightened being; ranked above gifts of food and wealth.
Impermanent, perishable; Dadhichi calls the body अनित्य and therefore no loss when given for others.
A cloud, literally 'water-carrier'; in the verse, clouds nourish crops they never eat — a model of selflessness.
Wealth, power, glory; सतां विभूतयः — the riches of the good exist for the service of others.
Free from disease, healthy; from the prayer सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः — may all be free from illness.
A form derived from a verbal root by a कृत् suffix, e.g. उक्त्वा (क्त्वा), प्रणम्य (ल्यप्), हन्तुम् (तुमुन्), निर्मितम् (क्त).

worksheet.title: Worksheet — परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 8)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give explanations in English. Refer to the story and verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Translate into simple English: "धन्यः अहम्, यत् मम अस्थिभिः लोकरक्षा भविष्यति।"
questions.answer: "Blessed (fortunate) am I, that by my bones the protection of the world will come about." Dadhichi counts himself lucky, not unlucky, that his bones will save the world.
questions.explanation: धन्यः = blessed; अस्थिभिः = by/with the bones (तृतीया); लोकरक्षा = protection of the world.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of each: अस्थि, वज्रम्, शरणम्, अत्याचारः, अनित्यम्.
questions.answer: अस्थि = bone; वज्रम् = thunderbolt (Indra's weapon); शरणम् = refuge/shelter; अत्याचारः = tyranny, atrocity; अनित्यम् = impermanent, perishable.
questions.explanation: All five words occur in the Dadhichi story of this lesson.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) आत्मोत्सर्गः (b) महर्षिः, and name the sandhi in each.
questions.answer: (a) आत्मोत्सर्गः = आत्मा + उत्सर्गः (आ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि). (b) महर्षिः = महा + ऋषिः (आ + ऋ = अर्, गुण-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Both are गुण-सन्धि: a simple vowel following अ/आ is replaced by its guna grade (ओ, अर्).

questions.question: Arrange the main events of the Dadhichi story in correct order, in 4-5 short sentences.
questions.answer: 1. Vritra obtained a boon that no ordinary weapon — dry or wet, of wood, stone or metal — could kill him, and tyrannised the three worlds. 2. The defeated gods, led by Indra, took refuge with Vishnu. 3. Vishnu revealed that only a vajra made from sage Dadhichi's bones could slay Vritra. 4. Indra humbly begged Dadhichi, who joyfully gave up his body by yoga. 5. Vishvakarma forged the vajra from the bones, and Indra slew Vritra, restoring peace.
questions.explanation: Boon → tyranny → refuge with Vishnu → Vishnu's counsel → Dadhichi's gift → vajra → Vritra slain.

questions.question: Dadhichi smiled (स्मित्वा) before agreeing to give his bones. What does this smile reveal about the nature of true sacrifice?
questions.answer: The smile shows that Dadhichi's sacrifice was completely willing and joyful, without hesitation, fear or regret. He saw the body as अनित्य (impermanent) and its highest use as service; giving it परार्थे was for him not a loss but a privilege — 'धन्यः अहम्'. True sacrifice is not a grudging duty but a glad offering.
questions.explanation: The detail स्मित्वा marks the difference between forced surrender and joyous self-giving.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय and English meaning of: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् । परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् ॥
questions.answer: अन्वयः: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् (अस्ति) — परोपकारः पुण्याय (भवति), परपीडनं पापाय (भवति)। Meaning: In all the eighteen Puranas Vyasa has, in essence, two sayings — doing good to others leads to merit (पुण्य), and hurting others leads to sin (पाप).
questions.explanation: पुण्याय and पापाय are datives of purpose/result: 'leads to merit / sin'.

questions.question: "Dadhichi lives on today." Evaluate this statement with at least three modern examples of परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः.
questions.answer: The statement is true: Dadhichi's ideal — giving oneself for the good of others — is alive wherever people put the larger good above their own life or comfort. (1) Soldiers guard the nation's borders knowing they may die for people they will never meet, giving the अभयदान of security. (2) Organ and body donors, like Dadhichi, give their very bodies so that others may live and learn — the closest modern echo of the sage's gift of his bones. (3) Doctors, nurses and volunteers who serve during epidemics and disasters risk their own health for strangers. One may add those who donate blood, firefighters, and citizens who give time and wealth for public causes. In each case the body or comfort is treated as अनित्य and the welfare of others (लोककल्याणम्) as the higher value — exactly Dadhichi's reasoning. Hence his story is not mere mythology but a living ideal of citizenship and humanity.
questions.explanation: Expect the principle (larger good above self) plus three well-explained modern parallels.

questions.question: Retell the story of महर्षि दधीचि in your own words (8-10 sentences) and state its moral.
questions.answer: Long ago the mighty asura Vritra performed severe austerity and won a boon: no ordinary weapon — dry or wet, of wood, stone or metal — could kill him. Made arrogant by the boon, he conquered heaven, drove out the gods and tormented the three worlds. The helpless gods, led by Indra, took refuge with Lord Vishnu. Vishnu told them that Vritra could be slain only by a vajra fashioned from the bones of sage Dadhichi, which the power of tapas had made harder than any weapon. The gods went to Dadhichi's hermitage in the Naimisha forest, where Indra bowed humbly and begged the sage's bones for the welfare of the world. Dadhichi smiled and replied that the body is impermanent, and that he was blessed that his bones would protect the world, for there is no dharma higher than परोपकार. He entered samadhi and gave up his life-breaths by yoga. Vishvakarma, the divine craftsman, forged the vajra from his bones, and with it Indra slew Vritra. Peace returned to the three worlds, and Dadhichi's name became a synonym for self-sacrifice. Moral: the body perishes, but the good done through it endures; self-sacrifice for others is the crown of all virtues, and true strength is born of tapas and tyaga.
questions.explanation: Full sequence of events in the student's own words plus a clearly stated moral.

questions.question: Who fashioned the vajra from Dadhichi's bones?
questions.answer: विश्वकर्मा
questions.explanation: Vishvakarma, the architect of the gods (देवशिल्पी), forged the vajra; Indra then wielded it.

questions.question: Translate into English: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः ।
questions.answer: May all be happy; may all be free from disease (illness).
questions.explanation: सुखिनः = happy; निरामयाः = free from disease; भवन्तु / सन्तु are third-person plural imperatives of blessing.

questions.question: The word परार्थे means
questions.answer: for the sake of others
questions.explanation: पर (other) + अर्थे (for the sake of) — the adverbial locative meaning 'for the sake of others'.

questions.question: आत्मोत्सर्गः is best translated as
questions.answer: the offering up of oneself
questions.explanation: आत्मा (self) + उत्सर्गः (giving up, release) = self-sacrifice, the offering up of oneself.

questions.question: According to the lesson, which gift stands at the very top of the ladder of दानम्?
questions.answer: आत्मदानम् — the gift of oneself
questions.explanation: Food sustains for a day, knowledge for a lifetime, protection longer still — but the gift of oneself holds nothing back and is supreme.

questions.question: अभयदानम् means the gift of
questions.answer: fearlessness (protection)
questions.explanation: अभय = absence of fear; अभयदानम् is the gift of protection/security to a frightened being.

questions.question: In the sentence परोपकारात् परः धर्मः नास्ति, Dadhichi declares that
options: there is no dharma higher than doing good to others
others should perform dharma for us
dharma and paropakara are both useless
questions.answer: there is no dharma higher than doing good to others
questions.explanation: परोपकारात् परः = higher than paropakara; नास्ति = there is not — service to others is the highest dharma.

questions.question: The opposite of परोपकारः, which Vyasa says leads to sin, is
questions.answer: परपीडनम्
questions.explanation: परपीडनम् = tormenting/hurting others; परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्.

questions.question: Which of the following actions would the lesson NOT count as a form of आत्मोत्सर्गः?
options: donating money publicly only to win praise and votes
a soldier guarding the border at the risk of his life
pledging one's organs so that others may live
a doctor serving patients in an epidemic at personal risk
questions.answer: donating money publicly only to win praise and votes
questions.explanation: आत्मोत्सर्ग is giving for the sake of OTHERS (परार्थे); giving merely for one's own fame is self-interest, not self-sacrifice.

questions.question: Dadhichi calls the body अनित्यम् in order to show that
options: the perishable body is best used in service of others
the body must be protected at all costs
the body is eternal like the soul
questions.answer: the perishable body is best used in service of others
questions.explanation: Since the body must perish anyway, its highest use is to be offered परार्थे — for the good of others.

questions.question: वृत्रः कः आसीत्? (Who was Vritra?)
questions.answer: महाबलः असुरः
questions.explanation: Vritra was a mighty asura (demon) — वृत्रः नाम महाबलः असुरः आसीत्।

questions.question: According to his boon, Vritra could NOT be killed by any weapon that was
options: of wood, stone or metal, whether dry or wet
questions.answer: of wood, stone or metal, whether dry or wet
questions.explanation: The boon excluded all ordinary weapons — शुष्केण वा आर्द्रेण वा, काष्ठेन वा पाषाणेन वा, लोहेन वा.

questions.question: भीताः देवाः कं शरणं गताः? (To whom did the frightened gods go for refuge?)
questions.answer: विष्णुम्
questions.explanation: The gods with Indra went to Lord Vishnu for refuge — भगवन्तं विष्णुं शरणं गताः।

questions.question: Whose bones alone could form the weapon to slay Vritra?
questions.answer: दधीचेः
questions.explanation: Vishnu said only a vajra made from sage Dadhichi's bones could kill Vritra.

questions.question: दधीचिः कः आसीत्?
questions.answer: महर्षिः (a great sage)
questions.explanation: Dadhichi was a great sage (महर्षि) practising tapas in the Naimisha forest.

questions.question: The weapon fashioned from Dadhichi's bones was the
questions.answer: वज्रम् (thunderbolt)
questions.explanation: Vishvakarma forged the vajra (thunderbolt), Indra's weapon, from the sage's bones.

questions.question: वज्रं केन निर्मितम्? (By whom was the vajra fashioned?)
questions.answer: विश्वकर्मणा
questions.explanation: Vishvakarma, the architect of the gods (देवशिल्पी), crafted the vajra.

questions.question: वृत्रः केन हतः? (By whom was Vritra slain?)
questions.answer: इन्द्रेण
questions.explanation: Indra slew Vritra with the vajra — तेन वज्रेण देवेन्द्रः वृत्रम् अहन्।

questions.question: How did Dadhichi give up his body?
questions.answer: by yoga, entering samadhi
questions.explanation: सः समाधिं गत्वा योगेन प्राणान् अत्यजत् — he entered samadhi and released his life-breaths by yoga.

questions.question: In which forest was Dadhichi's hermitage, according to the lesson?
questions.answer: नैमिषारण्ये
questions.explanation: Vishnu says: नैमिषारण्ये दधीचिः नाम महर्षिः तपः चरति — in the Naimisha forest.

questions.question: The vajra made from Dadhichi's bones is already alluded to in which ancient text?
questions.explanation: The legend of Dadhyanc/Dadhichi's bones appears in the Rigveda (1.84) and is retold in the Mahabharata and Puranas.

questions.question: What did Vritra do after conquering heaven?
options: He drove the gods out (देवान् निरवासयत्)
He crowned Indra as his minister
He returned heaven to the gods
questions.answer: He drove the gods out (देवान् निरवासयत्)
questions.explanation: वृत्रः स्वर्गं जित्वा देवान् निरवासयत् — having conquered heaven he exiled the gods.

questions.question: For what purpose did Indra say the gods were begging Dadhichi's bones?
options: लोककल्याणाय — for the welfare of the world
स्वर्गसुखाय — for the pleasures of heaven
questions.answer: लोककल्याणाय — for the welfare of the world
questions.explanation: इन्द्रः: लोककल्याणाय वयं भवतः अस्थीनि याचामहे — 'for the welfare of the world we beg your bones'.

questions.question: Why were the weapons of the gods useless against Vritra?
options: His boon protected him from all ordinary weapons
The gods had forgotten how to fight
His armour was made of vajra
He hid where no weapon could reach
questions.answer: His boon protected him from all ordinary weapons
questions.explanation: The boon excluded weapons of wood, stone and metal, dry or wet — so no ordinary weapon could even touch him.

questions.question: Why could Dadhichi's bones alone become the weapon against Vritra?
options: The power of his tapas had made them firmer than any weapon
They were made of celestial iron
They were the oldest bones in the world
questions.answer: The power of his tapas had made them firmer than any weapon
questions.explanation: तस्य अस्थीनि तपसा वज्रादपि दृढानि — by tapas his bones had become harder than even the thunderbolt, and they were no 'ordinary weapon' of wood, stone or metal.

questions.question: Why did Dadhichi call himself धन्यः (blessed)?
options: Because his bones would protect the world
Because the gods promised him heaven
Because he would be freed from tapas
questions.answer: Because his bones would protect the world
questions.explanation: धन्यः अहम्, यत् मम अस्थिभिः लोकरक्षा भविष्यति — he counted the chance to save the world a blessing, not a loss.

questions.question: Indra made his request सविनयं प्रणम्य (bowing with humility). This detail shows that
options: even the king of the gods must bow before a selfless sage
Indra was afraid Dadhichi would curse him
questions.answer: even the king of the gods must bow before a selfless sage
questions.explanation: The tapasvi's moral greatness outranks Indra's throne; power bows before renunciation.

questions.question: In the lesson, Vritra best symbolises
questions.answer: arrogant, tyrannical power (अधर्मः)
questions.explanation: वरगर्वितः — made arrogant by his boon, Vritra stands for adharmic power that torments the world and must be overcome.

questions.question: The deeper symbolism of the vajra being made from a sage's bones is that
options: true strength is born of tapas and sacrifice, not of metal
bones are physically stronger than iron
weapons should always be made by sages
the gods could not afford metal weapons
questions.answer: true strength is born of tapas and sacrifice, not of metal
questions.explanation: The mightiest weapon in the universe was made not of any metal but of a life of austerity and a moment of supreme self-giving.

questions.question: Why did Indra admit एषा याचना कठोरा (this request is cruel)?
options: Because he was asking the sage to give up his very life
Because the journey to the ashrama was difficult
Because Dadhichi was known to be miserly
Because the gods had no gift to offer in return
questions.answer: Because he was asking the sage to give up his very life
questions.explanation: To beg a man's bones is to beg his death; Indra acknowledges the harshness while pleading there is no other way (अन्यः उपायः नास्ति).

questions.question: What was the result of Vritra's slaying, according to the story?
options: Peace returned to the three worlds
A new asura arose at once
Indra gave up his throne to Dadhichi's son
questions.answer: Peace returned to the three worlds
questions.explanation: पुनः त्रिषु लोकेषु शान्तिः अभवत् — peace was restored in the three worlds.

questions.question: दधीचेः नाम आत्मोत्सर्गस्य पर्यायः इव स्मर्यते means that Dadhichi's name
options: is remembered as a very synonym of self-sacrifice
is used only in grammar books
questions.answer: is remembered as a very synonym of self-sacrifice
questions.explanation: पर्यायः = synonym; his very name now stands for आत्मोत्सर्ग.

questions.question: Dadhichi's words इदं शरीरं त्यक्तुं न कोऽपि शोकः express
options: that he feels no sorrow at all in giving up the body for others
his deep grief at leaving the world
his anger at the gods' request
questions.answer: that he feels no sorrow at all in giving up the body for others
questions.explanation: त्यक्तुम् = to give up; न कोऽपि शोकः = no sorrow whatsoever — the mark of a willing, joyful sacrifice.

questions.question: The gods' cry त्रायस्व नः त्रायस्व and Dadhichi's calm reply together contrast
questions.answer: helpless fear with fearless self-possession
questions.explanation: The mighty gods beg 'save us!', while the frail sage faces death smiling — moral strength outshines physical power.

questions.question: अस्थि इत्यस्य पदस्य अर्थः कः?
questions.answer: bone
questions.explanation: अस्थि = bone; plural अस्थीनि = bones.

questions.question: शरणम् means
questions.answer: refuge, shelter
questions.explanation: शरणं गताः = went for refuge; शरणम् = refuge/shelter.

questions.question: अत्याचारः इत्यस्य आङ्ग्लभाषायाम् अर्थः
questions.answer: tyranny, atrocity
questions.explanation: वृत्रस्य अत्याचारेण = by Vritra's tyranny/atrocities.

questions.question: The word वारिवाहः literally means 'water-carrier' and refers to
questions.answer: a cloud
questions.explanation: वारि (water) + वाहः (carrier) = cloud, which carries and gives rain.

questions.question: निरामयः means
questions.answer: free from disease
questions.explanation: निः (without) + आमय (disease) = healthy, free from illness; सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः.

questions.question: आश्रमः इत्यस्य अर्थः
questions.answer: hermitage
questions.explanation: आश्रमः = the hermitage/abode of a sage; देवाः दधीचेः आश्रमं गताः.

questions.question: समाधिः in the story refers to
questions.answer: deep meditative absorption
questions.explanation: सः समाधिं गत्वा — he entered deep yogic absorption before releasing his life-breaths.

questions.question: विभूतिः, as in सतां विभूतयः, means
questions.answer: riches, powers, glory
questions.explanation: सतां विभूतयः परोपकाराय — the riches/powers of the good exist for serving others.

questions.question: सस्यम् means
questions.answer: crop, grain
questions.explanation: नादन्ति सस्यं खलु वारिवाहाः — clouds do not eat the crops (they water).

questions.question: दुःखभाक् means
options: one who causes sorrow to others
questions.answer: a sharer/partaker of sorrow
questions.explanation: दुःखं भजते इति दुःखभाक् — one who partakes of sorrow; मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग्भवेत् = may no one come to sorrow.

questions.question: उपायः, as in अन्यः उपायः नास्ति, means
questions.answer: means, way
questions.explanation: 'There is no other means/way' of saving the world — अन्यः उपायः नास्ति.

questions.question: अम्भः, as in नाम्भः पिबन्ति, means
questions.answer: water
questions.explanation: अम्भः = water; rivers do not drink their own water — न अम्भः पिबन्ति.

questions.question: In the verse पिबन्ति नद्यः स्वयमेव नाम्भः..., the rivers, trees and clouds together illustrate that
options: nature keeps nothing for itself — its riches exist for others
nature is wasteful with its resources
only humans are capable of selfishness
rivers and clouds are living gods
questions.answer: nature keeps nothing for itself — its riches exist for others
questions.explanation: Rivers do not drink their water, trees do not eat their fruit, clouds do not eat crops — परोपकाराय सतां विभूतयः.

questions.question: वृक्षाः स्वयं किं न खादन्ति? (What do trees themselves not eat?)
questions.answer: फलानि
questions.explanation: स्वयं न खादन्ति फलानि वृक्षाः — trees do not eat their own fruits.

questions.question: In the verse त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे..., what should one give up for the sake of the village (ग्रामस्यार्थे)?
questions.answer: कुलम् (the family)
questions.explanation: The ladder runs: individual for family, family for village, village for country, everything for the Self.

questions.question: According to त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे..., what may one give up आत्मार्थे (for the sake of the Self)?
questions.answer: पृथिवीम् (the whole earth)
questions.explanation: आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् — for the highest Self even the whole earth may be renounced.

questions.question: According to the verse अष्टादशपुराणेषु..., Vyasa's two sayings are: परोपकारः पुण्याय and
questions.answer: पापाय परपीडनम्
questions.explanation: Helping others leads to merit; hurting others leads to sin — the essence of the eighteen Puranas.

questions.question: In परोपकारः पुण्याय, the dative पुण्याय expresses
questions.answer: result/purpose — 'leads to merit'
questions.explanation: The चतुर्थी of purpose/result: paropakara is FOR (i.e. results in) punya; likewise परपीडनम् पापाय.

questions.question: वज्रादपि कठोराणि मृदूनि कुसुमादपि describes the hearts of the great as
options: harder than the thunderbolt yet softer than a flower
questions.answer: harder than the thunderbolt yet softer than a flower
questions.explanation: लोकोत्तराणां चेतांसि — the hearts of extraordinary people combine vajra-hard resolve with flower-soft compassion.

questions.question: Why does the verse वज्रादपि कठोराणि... fit Dadhichi so exactly?
options: His heart was flower-soft in compassion but vajra-hard in resolve at the moment of sacrifice
He was afraid of the thunderbolt
He refused the gods with hard words
questions.answer: His heart was flower-soft in compassion but vajra-hard in resolve at the moment of sacrifice
questions.explanation: He melted with pity for the tormented worlds (soft as कुसुम) yet gave up his body without flinching (hard as वज्र) — and his bones became the vajra itself.

questions.question: The prayer सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः asks that ALL beings be
questions.answer: happy
questions.explanation: सर्वे = all; भवन्तु = may they be; सुखिनः = happy.

questions.question: मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग्भवेत् means
options: may no one be a partaker of sorrow
may everyone learn to bear sorrow
may sorrow come only to the wicked
questions.answer: may no one be a partaker of sorrow
questions.explanation: मा ... भवेत् = may (he) not be; कश्चित् = anyone; दुःखभाक् = sharer of sorrow.

questions.question: The word लोकोत्तराणाम् (लोक + उत्तर) literally describes people who are
questions.answer: beyond the ordinary world — extraordinary
questions.explanation: लोकोत्तर = beyond (उत्तर) the common world (लोक); hence 'extraordinary, superhuman' — whose hearts none can fathom.

questions.question: आत्मोत्सर्गः इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.answer: आत्मा + उत्सर्गः
questions.explanation: आ + उ = ओ (गुण-सन्धि): आत्मा + उत्सर्गः = आत्मोत्सर्गः.

questions.question: महर्षिः इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.answer: महा + ऋषिः
questions.explanation: आ + ऋ = अर् (गुण-सन्धि): महा + ऋषिः = महर्षिः.

questions.question: पर + उपकारः joins to form परोपकारः by which sandhi?
questions.answer: गुण-सन्धिः (अ + उ = ओ)
questions.explanation: अ followed by उ becomes ओ — guna sandhi, exactly as in आत्मोत्सर्गः.

questions.question: देवेन्द्रः इत्यस्य सन्धि-विच्छेदः कः?
questions.answer: देव + इन्द्रः
questions.explanation: अ + इ = ए (गुण-सन्धि): देव + इन्द्रः = देवेन्द्रः, 'Indra, lord of the gods'.

questions.question: वज्रादपि is formed from वज्रात् + अपि by which change?
questions.answer: त् → द् (जश्त्व, व्यञ्जन-सन्धिः)
questions.explanation: A final voiceless त् becomes voiced द् before a vowel: वज्रात् + अपि = वज्रादपि.

questions.question: नाम्भः (in पिबन्ति नद्यः स्वयमेव नाम्भः) splits as
questions.answer: न + अम्भः
questions.explanation: अ + अ = आ (दीर्घ-सन्धि): न + अम्भः = नाम्भः, 'not ... water'.

questions.question: परोपकारः = परेषाम् उपकारः is which समासः?
questions.answer: षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः
questions.explanation: The first member stands in the genitive (परेषाम्) relation to the second — genitive tatpurusha.

questions.question: महाबलः, explained as महत् बलं यस्य सः (Vritra, 'whose strength is great'), is which समासः?
questions.answer: बहुव्रीहिः
questions.explanation: The compound denotes a THIRD thing (the person whose strength is great) — the mark of bahuvrihi.

questions.question: In लोककल्याणाय वयं भवतः अस्थीनि याचामहे, the word लोककल्याणाय is in which विभक्तिः?
questions.answer: चतुर्थी (dative of purpose)
questions.explanation: The dative expresses purpose: 'FOR the welfare of the world'.

questions.question: In मम अस्थिभिः लोकरक्षा भविष्यति, the word अस्थिभिः is
questions.answer: तृतीया बहुवचनम् — 'by/with the bones'
questions.explanation: The instrumental plural -भिः shows the means: protection will come about BY the bones.

questions.question: उक्त्वा ('having spoken') is formed with which कृत्-suffix?
questions.answer: क्त्वा
questions.explanation: वच् + क्त्वा = उक्त्वा; the ktva suffix means 'having done X' (no prefix on the root).

questions.question: प्रणम्य ('having bowed') uses ल्यप् rather than क्त्वा because
options: the root has a prefix (प्र), and prefixed roots take ल्यप्
the root ends in a vowel
the word is in the passive voice
ल्यप् is used only for verbs of motion
questions.answer: the root has a prefix (प्र), and prefixed roots take ल्यप्
questions.explanation: Rule: with an upasarga (prefix), the gerund takes ल्यप् (-य): प्र + णम् + ल्यप् = प्रणम्य; without a prefix, क्त्वा (e.g. नत्वा).

questions.question: हन्तुम् ('in order to kill'), as in वृत्रः हन्तुं शक्यः, is formed with the suffix
questions.answer: तुमुन्
questions.explanation: हन् + तुमुन् = हन्तुम्, the infinitive of purpose: 'to kill'.

questions.question: निर्मितम् ('fashioned, made'), as in अस्थिभिः निर्मितं वज्रम्, is which kind of form?
questions.answer: क्त-प्रत्ययान्तः past passive participle
questions.explanation: निर् + मा/मि + क्त = निर्मित — 'that which has been fashioned'; it agrees with वज्रम् in gender and case.

questions.question: Which modern act is the CLOSEST parallel to Dadhichi's gift of his bones?
options: pledging one's organs and body for transplant and medical study after death
planting a tree in one's own garden
teaching a friend before an examination
questions.answer: pledging one's organs and body for transplant and medical study after death
questions.explanation: Like Dadhichi, the organ/body donor gives the body itself so that others may live — the most literal modern आत्मोत्सर्ग.

questions.question: The ladder in त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे... implies which principle for resolving conflicts of interest?
options: the smaller good must yield to the larger good
the individual always outweighs the community
the family must never be given up for anything
all interests are equal and none should yield
questions.answer: the smaller good must yield to the larger good
questions.explanation: Each rung sacrifices the narrower interest for the wider one — individual < family < village < country < the highest Self.

questions.question: Vritra's tapas won him a boon; Dadhichi's tapas hardened his bones. The lesson contrasts them to show that
options: the worth of power depends on whether it serves self or others
tapas always corrupts the one who performs it
questions.answer: the worth of power depends on whether it serves self or others
questions.explanation: The same austerity produced a tyrant's shield in Vritra and the world's salvation in Dadhichi — motive, not power, decides moral worth.

questions.question: Translate: देवाः दधीचेः आश्रमं गताः।
options: The gods went to Dadhichi's hermitage.
The gods drove Dadhichi from the hermitage.
Dadhichi went to the gods' palace.
The gods built a hermitage for Dadhichi.
questions.answer: The gods went to Dadhichi's hermitage.
questions.explanation: देवाः (the gods) दधीचेः (of Dadhichi) आश्रमम् (to the hermitage) गताः (went).

questions.question: Translate: सः योगेन प्राणान् अत्यजत्।
options: He gave up his life-breaths by yoga.
He obtained long life through yoga.
He taught yoga to save lives.
He abandoned yoga at the end of his life.
questions.answer: He gave up his life-breaths by yoga.
questions.explanation: योगेन (by yoga, instrumental) प्राणान् (life-breaths, object) अत्यजत् (gave up, past tense).

questions.question: Translate: तेन वज्रेण देवेन्द्रः वृत्रम् अहन्।
options: With that vajra Indra slew Vritra.
That vajra slew Indra and Vritra.
Indra gave that vajra to Vritra.
Vritra slew Indra with that vajra.
questions.answer: With that vajra Indra slew Vritra.
questions.explanation: तेन वज्रेण = with that vajra (instrumental); देवेन्द्रः = Indra (subject); वृत्रम् = Vritra (object); अहन् = slew.

questions.question: वृत्रः देवः आसीत्। (Vritra was a god.)
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: Vritra was a mighty असुर (demon), not a god — वृत्रः नाम महाबलः असुरः आसीत्।

questions.question: दधीचिः स्वेच्छया प्रसन्नमनसा च स्वानि अस्थीनि दत्तवान्। (Dadhichi gave his bones willingly and with a glad mind.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: He smiled (स्मित्वा), called himself blessed (धन्यः अहम्), and gave up his body by yoga without any sorrow.

questions.question: वज्रं विश्वकर्मणा निर्मितम्। (The vajra was fashioned by Vishvakarma.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: Vishvakarma, the architect of the gods, forged the vajra from Dadhichi's bones.

questions.question: Vritra was finally slain by Lord Vishnu himself.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: Vishnu only revealed the means; it was Indra (देवेन्द्रः) who slew Vritra with the vajra.

questions.question: According to Vyasa's verse, परोपकारः leads to पापम् (sin).
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: It is the reverse: परोपकारः पुण्याय (merit), पापाय परपीडनम् — hurting others leads to sin.

questions.question: आत्मोत्सर्गः इति पदे गुण-सन्धिः अस्ति। (The word आत्मोत्सर्गः contains guna sandhi.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: आत्मा + उत्सर्गः: आ + उ = ओ, which is गुण-सन्धि.

questions.question: The prayer सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः asks for happiness only for one's own family.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: सर्वे means ALL — the prayer embraces all beings, not any one family or group.

questions.question: अस्थि इत्यस्य अर्थः 'bone' इति। (The word अस्थि means 'bone'.)
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: अस्थि = bone; plural अस्थीनि — the bones Dadhichi donated.

questions.question: The legend of the vajra made from Dadhichi's bones is already alluded to in the Rigveda.
questions.answer: True
questions.explanation: The story of Dadhyanc (Dadhichi) appears in the Rigveda (1.84) and is retold in the Mahabharata and Puranas.

questions.question: According to त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे..., one should sacrifice the whole village for the sake of a single person.
questions.answer: False
questions.explanation: The ladder runs the other way: the narrower interest yields to the wider — one person for the family, the family for the village, the village for the country.

questions.question: दधीचेः अस्थिभिः निर्मितम् इन्द्रस्य आयुधं ________ इति कथ्यते। (Indra's weapon made from Dadhichi's bones is called ________.)
questions.answer: वज्रम्
questions.explanation: The thunderbolt (वज्रम्) was fashioned from the sage's bones.

questions.question: वज्रं देवशिल्पी ________ निर्ममे। (The vajra was fashioned by the divine craftsman ________.)
questions.answer: विश्वकर्मा
questions.explanation: विश्वकर्मा, the architect of the gods, forged the vajra.

questions.question: तेन वज्रेण ________ वृत्रम् अहन्। (With that vajra ________ slew Vritra.)
questions.answer: इन्द्रः
questions.explanation: Indra (देवेन्द्रः) slew Vritra with the vajra.

questions.question: भीताः देवाः भगवन्तं ________ शरणं गताः। (The frightened gods went for refuge to Lord ________.)
questions.answer: विष्णुम्
questions.explanation: The gods took refuge with Lord Vishnu — भगवन्तं विष्णुं शरणं गताः।

questions.question: पिबन्ति ________ स्वयमेव नाम्भः। (________ do not themselves drink their water.)
questions.answer: नद्यः
questions.explanation: Rivers (नद्यः) do not drink their own water — the opening of the paropakara verse.

questions.question: परोपकाराय सतां ________। (For the service of others are the ________ of the good.)
questions.answer: विभूतयः
questions.explanation: सतां विभूतयः — the riches/powers of the good exist for others.

questions.question: परोपकारः ________ पापाय परपीडनम्। (Helping others leads to ________; hurting others leads to sin.)
questions.answer: पुण्याय
questions.explanation: परोपकारः पुण्याय — doing good to others leads to merit (पुण्य).

questions.question: सर्वे भवन्तु ________ सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः। (May all be ________; may all be free from disease.)
questions.answer: सुखिनः
questions.explanation: सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः — may all be happy.

questions.question: सर्वे सन्तु ________ — may all be free from disease.
questions.answer: निरामयाः
questions.explanation: निरामयाः = free from disease (निः + आमय).

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदः: महर्षिः = महा + ________।
questions.answer: ऋषिः
questions.explanation: महा + ऋषिः = महर्षिः (आ + ऋ = अर्, गुण-सन्धि).

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदः: आत्मोत्सर्गः = आत्मा + ________।
questions.answer: उत्सर्गः
questions.explanation: आत्मा + उत्सर्गः = आत्मोत्सर्गः (आ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि).

questions.question: त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे... आत्मार्थे ________ त्यजेत्। (For the sake of the Self one may give up the ________.)
questions.answer: पृथिवीम्
questions.explanation: आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् — for the highest Self even the whole earth may be renounced.

questions.question: वज्रादपि कठोराणि मृदूनि ________ अपि। (Harder than the vajra, softer than even a ________.)
questions.answer: कुसुमात्
questions.explanation: कुसुमात् अपि (कुसुमादपि) = than even a flower; the ablative of comparison.

questions.question: दधीचिः समाधिं गत्वा ________ प्राणान् अत्यजत्। (Having entered samadhi, Dadhichi gave up his life-breaths by ________.)
questions.answer: योगेन
questions.explanation: योगेन = by yoga (instrumental) — the means by which he released his life.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेदः: परोपकारः = पर + ________।
questions.answer: उपकारः
questions.explanation: पर + उपकारः = परोपकारः (अ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि).

questions.question: Explain the meaning of the chapter title परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः, showing how each word contributes to the meaning.
questions.answer: परार्थे = पर (other) + अर्थे ('for the sake of', adverbial locative) — 'for the sake of others'. आत्मोत्सर्गः = आत्मा (one's self) + उत्सर्गः (offering up, giving up), joined by गुण-सन्धि (आ + उ = ओ). The title therefore means 'the offering up of oneself for the sake of others' — self-sacrifice for the good of others, the theme of the Dadhichi story.
questions.explanation: Both the derivation and the combined sense are expected.

questions.question: Describe the 'ladder of giving' (दानम्) mentioned in the lesson. Why is आत्मदानम् placed at the top?
questions.answer: The lesson ranks gifts in an ascending order: अन्नदानम् (gift of food) sustains a person for a day; विद्यादानम् (gift of knowledge) sustains for a lifetime; अभयदानम् (gift of fearlessness/protection) saves life itself; and आत्मदानम् or आत्मोत्सर्गः (gift of oneself) stands at the top. आत्मदान is supreme because in every other gift the giver parts with something he HAS, but in self-sacrifice he gives what he IS — nothing at all is held back, as Dadhichi held back nothing when he gave his very bones.
questions.explanation: The four rungs plus the reason — total self-giving — are expected.

questions.question: What does Dadhichi mean by saying परोपकारात् परः धर्मः नास्ति?
questions.answer: He means 'there is no dharma higher than doing good to others.' Among all duties and virtues, service to others stands highest; therefore giving his own body to save the worlds is, for him, not a loss but the very fulfilment of dharma.
questions.explanation: परोपकारात् = than paropakara (ablative of comparison); परः = higher; नास्ति = there is not.

questions.question: State the exact terms of Vritra's boon and explain how the vajra made from bones escaped those terms.
questions.answer: Vritra's boon said that he could not be slain by any ordinary weapon — whether dry (शुष्क) or wet (आर्द्र), whether made of wood (काष्ठ), stone (पाषाण) or metal (लोह). A vajra fashioned from a sage's bones is none of these: it is not wood, not stone, not metal, and being sanctified and hardened by tapas it is no 'ordinary weapon' at all. Hence the bone-vajra fell outside every term of the boon and could kill him.
questions.explanation: Both the boon's list and the loophole logic are required.

questions.question: What advice did Lord Vishnu give to the gods when they came to him for refuge?
questions.answer: Vishnu told them that Vritra could not be killed by ordinary weapons; in the Naimisha forest lives the great sage Dadhichi, whose bones have become harder than the vajra through tapas; only a thunderbolt fashioned from those bones can slay Vritra; therefore the gods should go and beg the sage for his bones.
questions.explanation: Four elements: no ordinary weapon; Dadhichi's tapas-hardened bones; vajra from them; go and beg.

questions.question: What role does Vishvakarma play in the story, and what is he called in Sanskrit?
questions.answer: Vishvakarma is the architect/craftsman of the gods, called देवशिल्पी in the lesson. After Dadhichi gave up his body, Vishvakarma fashioned (निर्ममे) the vajra out of the sage's bones, which Indra then used to slay Vritra.
questions.explanation: देवशिल्पी = craftsman of the gods; he is the maker of the weapon, not its wielder.

questions.question: Why does the lesson stress that Indra bowed सविनयम् (with humility) before Dadhichi? What does this teach about the relation between power and virtue?
questions.answer: Indra is the king of the gods, yet he bows humbly before a forest sage who owns nothing. The lesson stresses this to show that moral greatness outranks worldly power: the tapasvi who can give himself away for others is greater than the throne of heaven. Power must bow before virtue and renunciation; those who seek help for a noble cause must ask with humility, not command.
questions.explanation: The contrast between Indra's rank and his humility, and its lesson, are expected.

questions.question: In what sense is the vajra a symbol of the power of त्याग (sacrifice)?
questions.answer: The vajra — the mightiest weapon in the universe, before which even the invincible Vritra fell — was made not of iron or stone but of the bones of a man who gave himself away for others. Its strength came from a lifetime of tapas and a moment of supreme tyaga. Thus the vajra symbolises that sacrifice, not material, is the source of real, irresistible strength.
questions.explanation: Strength born of tapas and self-giving, not of metal.

questions.question: Contrast Vritra and Dadhichi as two uses of the power gained by tapas.
questions.answer: Both Vritra and Dadhichi acquired extraordinary power through austerity, but they used it in opposite ways. Vritra turned his boon into a shield for tyranny — वरगर्वितः, he conquered heaven, exiled the gods and tormented the three worlds; his power served only his ego. Dadhichi's tapas hardened his bones into a treasure, and he spent that treasure entirely on others, giving his body itself for लोककल्याण. The story thus teaches that power is morally neutral: directed to self, it becomes अधर्म; offered परार्थे, it becomes the salvation of the world.
questions.explanation: Same source (tapas), opposite uses (self vs others) — that antithesis is the heart of the lesson.

questions.question: Why does Dadhichi say इदं शरीरम् अनित्यम् अस्ति before agreeing to give his bones?
questions.answer: He reminds the gods (and himself) that the body is impermanent — it must decay and die in any case. Since it cannot be kept forever, the wisest use of it is to spend it for the good of others. The thought of the body's impermanence removes all sorrow (न कोऽपि शोकः) from the act of giving it up.
questions.explanation: अनित्यम् = impermanent; the premise that makes the sacrifice reasonable and sorrowless.

questions.question: Give the English शब्दार्थ of: तपः, वरः, शस्त्रम्, वधः, शान्तिः.
questions.answer: तपः = austerity/penance; वरः = boon; शस्त्रम् = weapon; वधः = killing/slaying; शान्तिः = peace.
questions.explanation: All five occur in the Dadhichi story.

questions.question: Give the English शब्दार्थ of: वारिवाहः, सस्यम्, विभूतिः, कुसुमम्, चेतांसि.
questions.answer: वारिवाहः = cloud (water-carrier); सस्यम् = crop/grain; विभूतिः = riches/power/glory; कुसुमम् = flower; चेतांसि = hearts/minds (plural of चेतस्).
questions.explanation: All five occur in the verses on tyaga and paropakara.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of पिबन्ति नद्यः स्वयमेव नाम्भः... and give its full English meaning.
questions.answer: अन्वयः: नद्यः स्वयम् एव अम्भः न पिबन्ति; वृक्षाः स्वयं फलानि न खादन्ति; वारिवाहाः खलु सस्यं न अदन्ति; सतां विभूतयः परोपकाराय (भवन्ति)। Meaning: Rivers do not drink their own water; trees do not eat their own fruits; clouds certainly do not eat the crops (they nourish); the riches of the good exist for the service of others.
questions.explanation: The anvaya restores prose order and supplies the understood verb भवन्ति.

questions.question: Explain the ladder of sacrifice taught in त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत्...
questions.answer: The verse arranges interests in widening circles: for the sake of the family one should give up one individual('s interest); for the sake of the village, the family; for the sake of the country (जनपद), the village; and for the sake of the Self — the highest truth — one may give up the whole earth. Each rung teaches that the narrower good must yield to the wider good, and that the supreme good (आत्मन्/धर्म) outweighs everything material.
questions.explanation: एकम् → कुलम् → ग्रामः → जनपदः → आत्मार्थे पृथिवीम् — the ascending order matters.

questions.question: Translate the verse सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः । सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग्भवेत् ॥ and state its central sentiment.
questions.answer: Translation: May all be happy; may all be free from disease; may all see auspicious things; may no one be a partaker of sorrow. Central sentiment: universal goodwill — the prayer asks for the welfare of ALL beings without exception, not for oneself or one's own group.
questions.explanation: The fourfold blessing and the universality (सर्वे) are the key points.

questions.question: Explain the paradox in वज्रादपि कठोराणि मृदूनि कुसुमादपि and show how the Dadhichi story resolves it.
questions.answer: The verse says the hearts of the truly great are at once harder than the thunderbolt and softer than a flower — an apparent contradiction. The Dadhichi story resolves it: his heart was flower-soft in compassion, melting at the suffering of the three worlds; yet vajra-hard in resolve, giving up his own body without a tremor when the sacrifice was needed. Softness governs the great in feeling for others; hardness governs them in demands upon themselves. Fittingly, this soft-hearted sage's bones became the hard vajra itself.
questions.explanation: Both poles (compassion/resolve) and their application to Dadhichi are expected.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) परोपकारः (b) देवेन्द्रः (c) नाम्भः.
questions.answer: (a) परोपकारः = पर + उपकारः (अ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि). (b) देवेन्द्रः = देव + इन्द्रः (अ + इ = ए, गुण-सन्धि). (c) नाम्भः = न + अम्भः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Two guna joins and one dirgha join, all from the lesson.

questions.question: Identify the कृदन्त suffix in each form and give its meaning: श्रुत्वा, प्रणम्य, त्यक्तुम्, पीडिताः.
questions.answer: श्रुत्वा — क्त्वा ('having heard'; unprefixed root श्रु). प्रणम्य — ल्यप् ('having bowed'; the prefix प्र forces ल्यप् instead of क्त्वा). त्यक्तुम् — तुमुन् (infinitive, 'to give up'). पीडिताः — क्त past passive participle ('tormented', masculine plural agreeing with लोकाः).
questions.explanation: क्त्वा vs ल्यप् (prefix rule), तुमुन् infinitive and क्त participle.

questions.question: The verse पिबन्ति नद्यः... calls nature the first teacher of परोपकार. Analyse how the three images of the verse apply to Dadhichi himself.
questions.answer: The river gives away all its water, keeping none — Dadhichi gave away his whole body, keeping nothing. The tree bears fruit that others eat — the sage's lifetime of tapas bore its final 'fruit', the bones, for others to use. The cloud pours rain on crops it will never taste — Dadhichi died for a world whose peace he would never live to see. In each image the possessor never enjoys its own wealth; likewise सतां विभूतयः परोपकाराय — the sage's one treasure, his tapas-hardened body, existed wholly for others.
questions.explanation: Mapping each natural image onto the sage's act shows analytical understanding.

questions.question: Give two modern examples of परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः and state, for each, what is being sacrificed and for whom.
questions.answer: Examples (any two): (1) A soldier at the border sacrifices personal safety, comfort and possibly life for the security of fellow citizens he has never met. (2) An organ/body donor sacrifices his or her body after death so that patients may live and students may learn — the closest parallel to Dadhichi. (3) Doctors, nurses and volunteers in an epidemic sacrifice their own health and rest for their patients. In each case a personal good (life, body, health) is given up for the wider good of others.
questions.explanation: Any two clear examples with the what-and-for-whom analysis.

questions.question: Translate into English: "भगवन्! वृत्रस्य अत्याचारेण त्रयः लोकाः पीडिताः सन्ति। लोककल्याणाय वयं भवतः अस्थीनि याचामहे।"
questions.answer: "Revered one! The three worlds are tormented by Vritra's tyranny. For the welfare of the world we beg of you your bones." (अत्याचारेण = by the tyranny, instrumental; पीडिताः सन्ति = are tormented; लोककल्याणाय = for the world's welfare, dative of purpose; याचामहे = we beg.)
questions.explanation: Indra's humble request at the hermitage; note the dative of purpose.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about परोपकार or त्याग, and give their English meanings.
questions.answer: Sample answer: 1. परोपकारः परमः धर्मः अस्ति। (Doing good to others is the highest dharma.) 2. वृक्षाः फलानि परेभ्यः यच्छन्ति। (Trees give their fruits to others.) 3. दधीचिः लोकहिताय स्वं शरीरम् अत्यजत्। (Dadhichi gave up his own body for the good of the world.) Any three grammatically correct sentences on the theme earn full marks.
questions.explanation: Simple subject-object-verb sentences using chapter vocabulary.

questions.question: "परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः is the crown of all virtues." Explain this ideal as presented in the lesson, describing the ladder of giving and showing why self-sacrifice stands above every other form of दानम्.
questions.answer: The lesson presents giving (दानम्) as a ladder of ever-greater gifts. अन्नदानम्, the gift of food, relieves hunger for a day; धनदानम् relieves want for a while; विद्यादानम्, the gift of knowledge, equips a person for a lifetime; अभयदानम्, the gift of fearlessness or protection, saves life itself. Yet in all these the giver parts only with something he possesses — food, money, learning, strength — while he himself remains safely intact. At the top of the ladder stands आत्मदानम् or आत्मोत्सर्गः (आत्मा + उत्सर्गः, by guna sandhi): the offering up of one's own self — comfort, body, even life — परार्थे, for the sake of others. It is the crown of virtues because here the giver and the gift become one; nothing whatever is held back. Dadhichi embodies this: he did not donate from his wealth, for he had none; he donated his very bones, treating the perishable body (अनित्यम् शरीरम्) as a trust to be spent for the world. All other virtues — truth, kindness, charity — reach their fulfilment in this readiness to give oneself; hence Vyasa's summary परोपकारः पुण्याय and Dadhichi's own words परोपकारात् परः धर्मः नास्ति.
questions.explanation: Expect the ladder (अन्न/विद्या/अभय/आत्म-दान), the giver-becomes-gift argument, and Dadhichi as the embodiment.

questions.question: Narrate the story of महर्षि दधीचि from Vritra's boon to the restoration of peace, and explain what each stage of the story contributes to the theme of self-sacrifice.
questions.answer: Stage 1 — The boon: Vritra's austerity wins him immunity from all ordinary weapons, dry or wet, of wood, stone or metal; power without goodness at once becomes tyranny (वरगर्वितः), showing why the world needs selfless protectors. Stage 2 — The tyranny: he conquers heaven and exiles the gods; even the mighty are helpless, proving that force alone cannot defeat adharma. Stage 3 — The refuge: the gods surrender their pride and seek Vishnu's counsel, teaching that humility precedes deliverance. Stage 4 — The counsel: only a vajra made of Dadhichi's tapas-hardened bones can slay Vritra; the remedy for selfish power is the fruit of selfless austerity. Stage 5 — The request: Indra bows humbly and begs the bones for लोककल्याण, admitting the request is cruel — the world's welfare sometimes demands the dearest price. Stage 6 — The gift: Dadhichi smiles, calls the body impermanent and himself blessed (धन्यः अहम्), and releases his life by yoga — the willing joy of the giver is the soul of true sacrifice. Stage 7 — The victory: Vishvakarma forges the vajra, Indra slays Vritra, peace returns to the three worlds — one man's self-gift becomes the salvation of all. The story ends with Dadhichi's name itself becoming a synonym (पर्यायः) of आत्मोत्सर्ग.
questions.explanation: Full narrative sequence plus the thematic point of each stage.

questions.question: Explain in detail any TWO of the following verses with अन्वय, word meanings and moral: (a) पिबन्ति नद्यः स्वयमेव नाम्भः... (b) अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम्... (c) वज्रादपि कठोराणि मृदूनि कुसुमादपि...
questions.answer: (a) अन्वयः: नद्यः स्वयम् एव अम्भः न पिबन्ति; वृक्षाः स्वयं फलानि न खादन्ति; वारिवाहाः खलु सस्यं न अदन्ति; सतां विभूतयः परोपकाराय। शब्दार्थ: अम्भः = water, वारिवाहाः = clouds, सस्यम् = crop, विभूतयः = riches. Meaning: rivers never drink their own water, trees never eat their own fruit, clouds never eat the crops they water — so the riches of the good exist for others. Moral: nature is the first teacher of selfless service. (b) अन्वयः: अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् — परोपकारः पुण्याय, परपीडनं पापाय। शब्दार्थ: वचनद्वयम् = two sayings, पुण्याय/पापाय = leading to merit/sin (datives of result), परपीडनम् = hurting others. Meaning: the whole teaching of the eighteen Puranas fits into two phrases — serving others earns merit, harming others earns sin. Moral: the entire dharma condensed: help, never hurt. (c) अन्वयः: लोकोत्तराणां चेतांसि वज्रात् अपि कठोराणि, कुसुमात् अपि मृदूनि; कः तानि विज्ञातुम् अर्हति? शब्दार्थ: लोकोत्तराणाम् = of the extraordinary, चेतांसि = hearts, कठोराणि = harder, मृदूनि = softer. Meaning: the hearts of the great are harder than the thunderbolt yet softer than a flower — who can fathom them? Moral: greatness unites flower-soft compassion for others with vajra-hard resolve toward oneself, exactly as in Dadhichi. (Any two fully explained earn full marks.)
questions.explanation: For each chosen verse: anvaya, key word meanings, translation and moral.

questions.question: "The vajra was not made of metal but of character." Evaluate this statement in the light of the Dadhichi story. What does it suggest about where a nation's real strength lies?
questions.answer: The statement is profoundly true to the story. Every metal weapon of the gods had failed: Vritra's boon made ordinary arms — wood, stone, metal, dry or wet — useless. What finally shattered his tyranny was a weapon whose raw material was a human life shaped by discipline: bones hardened by decades of tapas and surrendered in a moment of perfect selflessness. The physical vajra is thus a symbol; its true substance is त्याग and तपस् — character. The suggestion for a nation is clear: arsenals, wealth and technology are the 'metal' of national life, necessary but never sufficient. A nation's real strength lies in citizens of character — people willing to discipline themselves and, when the hour demands, to place the common good above private interest: the soldier, the honest official, the organ donor, the scientist or doctor who serves at personal cost. Where such Dadhichis exist, even scarce material resources become invincible vajras; where they are absent, the finest weapons defend nothing worth keeping. One may add the caution that such sacrifice must be voluntary and for a worthy cause — Dadhichi was begged, not compelled, and gave with a smile.
questions.explanation: Evaluation should link the failed metal weapons, the tapas-made vajra, and the generalisation to civic character.

questions.question: Analyse the ladder-principle of त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे... Does it justify sacrificing an individual against his will for the majority? Discuss with reference to Dadhichi's consent.
questions.answer: The verse teaches that when goods conflict, the narrower should yield to the wider: one (individual interest) for the family, the family for the village, the village for the country, and everything for the highest Self/dharma. Read carelessly, this might seem to justify a majority seizing an individual's life or property 'for the greater good'. The Dadhichi story guards against exactly that reading. The gods, though desperate, do not take the sage's bones by force or trickery; Indra bows humbly (सविनयं प्रणम्य), states the cause truthfully, admits the cruelty of the request (एषा याचना कठोरा), and waits for consent. The sacrifice acquires its moral worth precisely because Dadhichi chooses it freely and joyfully — स्वेच्छया, with a smile. Thus the ladder is a principle of self-ordering, telling ME which of MY interests to surrender first; it is not a licence for compulsion of others. Forced 'sacrifice' is merely परपीडनम्, which Vyasa's verse condemns as the road to sin. The ideal, therefore: institutions may ask, and honour those who give; but आत्मोत्सर्ग must remain आत्म — of the self, by the self.
questions.explanation: Expect: the ladder explained, the consent question raised, and the स्वेच्छया/परपीडनम् distinction.

questions.question: "Modern life offers no scope for Dadhichi's ideal." Argue for or against this view, giving at least four examples from contemporary life and connecting each to the lesson.
questions.answer: Against the view: the forms have changed, but the scope for परार्थे आत्मोत्सर्गः has never been wider. (1) Organ and body donation: a donor's pledge lets his eyes, heart or kidneys restore life to strangers — the direct modern echo of Dadhichi's bones becoming the world-saving vajra. (2) Armed forces and disaster responders: soldiers, firefighters and rescue workers accept possible death for people they will never meet — modern अभयदान. (3) Medical service in epidemics: doctors, nurses and sanitation workers who serve infectious patients spend their health for the public, like clouds raining on fields whose harvest they never eat (वारिवाहाः). (4) Everyday tyaga: blood donation, giving one's savings to educate poor children, whistle-blowing at the cost of one's career, even a scientist forgoing patents so medicine stays cheap — each puts the wider circle above the narrower, exactly as त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे prescribes. What the lesson adds is the spirit: such giving must be willing and glad (Dadhichi's smile), not grudging or forced. Since suffering, disease and injustice still exist, and since every person still owns a self that can be offered, the ideal is not obsolete; it is simply waiting for volunteers.
questions.explanation: A reasoned stand with four connected examples; the Dadhichi-smile criterion of willingness should appear.

questions.question: Translate the following passage into English and comment briefly on its language: "तत् श्रुत्वा महर्षिः ईषत् स्मित्वा अवदत् — हे देवाः! इदं शरीरम् अनित्यम् अस्ति। परार्थे इदं शरीरं त्यक्तुं न कोऽपि शोकः। धन्यः अहम्, यत् मम अस्थिभिः लोकरक्षा भविष्यति।"
questions.answer: Translation: "Hearing that, the great sage, smiling gently, said — 'O gods! This body is impermanent. To give up this body for the sake of others is no sorrow at all. Blessed am I, that by my bones the protection of the world will come about.'" Comment: the passage uses the gerund श्रुत्वा (क्त्वा, 'having heard') and स्मित्वा ('having smiled') to chain actions; the infinitive त्यक्तुम् (तुमुन्) expresses purpose ('to give up'); अनित्यम् is a predicate adjective with शरीरम्; अस्थिभिः is the instrumental plural of means ('by my bones'); and the यत्-clause gives the reason for धन्यः अहम्. The short, calm sentences mirror the sage's serenity: no lament, only glad acceptance.
questions.explanation: Accurate translation plus notice of the gerunds, infinitive, instrumental and the tone.

questions.question: Compose a short Sanskrit paragraph of 5-6 simple sentences (in Devanagari) on the topic परोपकारः, using at least four words from this lesson, and give its English translation.
questions.answer: Sample answer: परोपकारः परमः धर्मः अस्ति। वृक्षाः परेभ्यः फलानि यच्छन्ति। नद्यः सर्वेभ्यः जलं वहन्ति। दधीचिः लोककल्याणाय स्वानि अस्थीनि अपि दत्तवान्। तस्य आत्मोत्सर्गेण त्रयः लोकाः रक्षिताः। वयम् अपि परार्थे किञ्चित् त्यक्तुं यतामहै। Translation: Doing good to others is the highest dharma. Trees give fruits to others. Rivers carry water for all. Dadhichi gave even his own bones for the welfare of the world. By his self-sacrifice the three worlds were saved. Let us too strive to give up something for the sake of others. (Any grammatically correct paragraph on the theme using lesson vocabulary — e.g. परोपकारः, अस्थीनि, लोककल्याणाय, आत्मोत्सर्गः, त्यक्तुम् — earns full marks.)
questions.explanation: Assess grammar (agreement, vibhakti), use of lesson vocabulary and coherence of the paragraph.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
"पुरा वृत्रः नाम महाबलः असुरः आसीत्। सः उग्रं तपः तप्त्वा वरं प्राप्तवान् — काष्ठेन वा पाषाणेन वा लोहेन वा केनापि सामान्येन शस्त्रेण मम वधः मा भवतु इति। वरगर्वितः सः त्रीन् लोकान् अपीडयत्।"
(a) वृत्रः कः आसीत्? (b) सः वरं कथं प्राप्तवान्? (c) List the materials named in the boon. (d) What did Vritra do after receiving the boon?
questions.answer: (a) वृत्रः महाबलः असुरः आसीत् — Vritra was a mighty demon. (b) सः उग्रं तपः तप्त्वा वरं प्राप्तवान् — he obtained the boon by performing fierce austerity. (c) The boon names wood (काष्ठ), stone (पाषाण) and metal (लोह) — no ordinary weapon of these could kill him. (d) Made arrogant by the boon (वरगर्वितः), he tormented the three worlds (त्रीन् लोकान् अपीडयत्).
questions.explanation: Direct comprehension of the opening of the story.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
"भगवान् अवदत् — नैमिषारण्ये दधीचिः नाम महर्षिः तपः चरति। तस्य अस्थीनि तपसा वज्रादपि दृढानि सन्ति। तैः अस्थिभिः निर्मितेन वज्रेण एव वृत्रः हन्तुं शक्यः। यूयं गत्वा तं महर्षिं याचध्वम्।"
(a) Who is speaking, and to whom? (b) दधीचिः कुत्र तपः चरति? (c) Why are Dadhichi's bones described as वज्रादपि दृढानि? (d) What command is given in याचध्वम्?
questions.answer: (a) Lord Vishnu (भगवान्) is speaking to the gods (with Indra) who came to him for refuge. (b) दधीचिः नैमिषारण्ये तपः चरति — in the Naimisha forest. (c) Because the power of his austerity (तपसा) has made them firmer than even the thunderbolt. (d) याचध्वम् is a plural imperative: 'go and beg (request) that great sage' — the gods are told to ask Dadhichi for his bones.
questions.explanation: Tests speaker identification, locative comprehension and the imperative form.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
"देवेन्द्रः सविनयं प्रणम्य अवदत् — भगवन्! लोककल्याणाय वयं भवतः अस्थीनि याचामहे। एषा याचना कठोरा इति जानीमः, परं लोकरक्षायाः अन्यः उपायः नास्ति।"
(a) How does Indra approach the sage, and why is this significant? (b) What exactly do the gods ask for, and for what purpose? (c) Why does Indra himself call the request कठोरा? (d) What justification does he offer for making it nonetheless?
questions.answer: (a) He approaches सविनयं प्रणम्य — bowing with humility; significant because even the king of the gods bows before a selfless sage, showing virtue outranks power. (b) They ask for Dadhichi's bones (भवतः अस्थीनि), for the welfare of the world (लोककल्याणाय). (c) Because granting it means the sage must give up his very life — to beg a man's bones is to beg his death. (d) That there is no other means of saving the world — लोकरक्षायाः अन्यः उपायः नास्ति; necessity, honestly admitted, is his only justification.
questions.explanation: Interpretive reading of Indra's request — humility, content, cruelty, necessity.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
"महर्षिः ईषत् स्मित्वा अवदत् — इदं शरीरम् अनित्यम् अस्ति। परार्थे इदं शरीरं त्यक्तुं न कोऽपि शोकः। धन्यः अहम्। इति उक्त्वा सः समाधिं गत्वा योगेन प्राणान् अत्यजत्।"
(a) What does the sage's slight smile (ईषत् स्मित्वा) convey? (b) On what reasoning does he base his consent? (c) Why does he call himself धन्यः rather than pitiable? (d) How does he give up his life, and what does that manner add to the meaning of his sacrifice?
questions.answer: (a) The smile conveys perfect willingness and inner peace — no fear, hesitation or regret. (b) That the body is impermanent (अनित्यम्) anyway, so giving it up for others (परार्थे) involves no real loss and hence no sorrow. (c) Because his bones will accomplish the protection of the world — he counts the opportunity to serve as a blessing, the highest fruit of his life of tapas. (d) He enters samadhi and releases his life-breaths by yoga (योगेन) — calm, deliberate self-mastery to the very end, showing the sacrifice is a sovereign act of his own will, not a death inflicted on him.
questions.explanation: The four details — smile, reasoning, dhanyah, yogic death — together define ideal sacrifice.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
"पिबन्ति नद्यः स्वयमेव नाम्भः स्वयं न खादन्ति फलानि वृक्षाः ।
नादन्ति सस्यं खलु वारिवाहाः परोपकाराय सतां विभूतयः ॥"
(a) Name the three givers of the verse and what each gives. (b) What is common to all three? (c) State the conclusion drawn in the fourth line.
questions.answer: (a) Rivers (नद्यः) give water; trees (वृक्षाः) give fruits; clouds (वारिवाहाः) give rain that grows the crops. (b) None of them consumes its own gift — the river does not drink its water, the tree does not eat its fruit, the cloud does not eat the crop. (c) Conclusion: परोपकाराय सतां विभूतयः — the riches/powers of the good exist for the service of others, just as nature's wealth does.
questions.explanation: Straightforward analysis of the verse's three images and its moral.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
"त्यजेदेकं कुलस्यार्थे ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत् ।
ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् ॥"
(a) Write the ladder of the verse in order, from smallest to largest. (b) What is the grammatical form and meaning of त्यजेत्? (c) How does आत्मार्थे in the last quarter differ in sense from the other अर्थे phrases? (d) Connect the verse to Dadhichi's act.
questions.answer: (a) One individual → family (कुल) → village (ग्राम) → country (जनपद) → and for the Self, even the whole earth (पृथिवी). (b) त्यजेत् is विधिलिङ् (optative), third person singular of त्यज् — 'one should give up'. (c) In the first three quarters अर्थे means 'for the sake of' a larger GROUP; आत्मार्थे points not to selfishness but to the highest Self/ultimate good, for which even the whole world may be renounced. (d) Dadhichi lived the ladder's logic to its summit: he gave up the narrowest good — his own body — for the widest circle of all, the welfare of the three worlds.
questions.explanation: Order, optative form, the special sense of आत्मन्, and the application to the story.

questions.question:
Read the situation and answer the questions:
Rohan, a Class 12 student, reads about a retired teacher who pledged her body to a medical college and her savings to a village library. His friend remarks, "Such sacrifice was possible only in the age of sages like Dadhichi; today everyone must look after himself first."
(a) Using the lesson, how should Rohan reply to his friend? (b) Which two elements of Dadhichi's sacrifice reappear in the teacher's pledge? (c) Which verse from the lesson best answers the friend's 'everyone for himself' attitude, and why?
questions.answer: (a) Rohan should reply that आत्मोत्सर्ग is not confined to any age: wherever a person freely gives his body, wealth or comfort for others' good, Dadhichi's ideal lives on — the teacher is proof standing before them. (b) First, the gift of the body itself (body pledged to the medical college, as Dadhichi's bones went to make the vajra); second, the willing, cheerful spirit — she pledged of her own accord, unforced, as Dadhichi gave with a smile. (c) पिबन्ति नद्यः... परोपकाराय सतां विभूतयः (or परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्) — because it declares that whatever the good possess exists for others, directly refuting the claim that one must live for oneself alone.
questions.explanation: Application of the ideal to a contemporary case with textual support.

questions.question:
Read the situation and answer the questions:
During a flood, boatman Karim rows all night rescuing stranded villagers, refusing payment. A news channel calls him 'the Dadhichi of the river'. His neighbour objects: "He did not give his life; the comparison is exaggerated."
(a) In what respects is the comparison apt? (b) In what respect does the neighbour have a point? (c) Does the lesson require the loss of life for an act to count as आत्मोत्सर्गः? Justify with the concept of the ladder of giving.
questions.answer: (a) Apt because Karim risked his life all night for strangers, sought no reward, and acted willingly and gladly — the spirit (परार्थे, स्वेच्छया) is exactly Dadhichi's. (b) The neighbour is right that the DEGREE differs: Dadhichi actually surrendered his life; Karim risked but kept his. (c) No — the lesson presents giving as a ladder: gifts of food, effort, protection (अभयदान) and finally the self. Every rung climbed परार्थे partakes of the same ideal; आत्मोत्सर्ग is its highest rung, not its only one. Karim's night of fearless service is real अभयदान and genuine self-offering of comfort and safety; the title honours the spirit, even if the summit of the ladder belongs to those who, like Dadhichi, give all.
questions.explanation: Distinguishing spirit vs degree of sacrifice using the dana ladder.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer in English:
"ततः विश्वकर्मा देवशिल्पी तस्य अस्थिभिः वज्रं निर्ममे। तेन वज्रेण देवेन्द्रः वृत्रम् अहन्। पुनः त्रिषु लोकेषु शान्तिः अभवत्।"
(a) Translate the passage. (b) Identify the विभक्ति of अस्थिभिः and of वज्रेण and state what each expresses.
questions.answer: (a) Translation: "Then Vishvakarma, the architect of the gods, fashioned the vajra from his (Dadhichi's) bones. With that vajra Indra slew Vritra. Peace arose again in the three worlds." (b) Both अस्थिभिः ('from/with the bones', plural) and वज्रेण ('with the vajra', singular) are in तृतीया विभक्ति (instrumental); each expresses the means/instrument by which the action was done — the bones as the material of making, the vajra as the instrument of slaying.
questions.explanation: Translation plus recognition of the instrumental of means in both words.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
"सर्वे भवन्तु सुखिनः सर्वे सन्तु निरामयाः ।
सर्वे भद्राणि पश्यन्तु मा कश्चिद् दुःखभाग्भवेत् ॥"
(a) Translate the verse into English. (b) Pick out the three imperative/benedictive verb forms and give their meanings. (c) In one sentence, say how this prayer relates to the theme of the chapter.
questions.answer: (a) Translation: May all be happy; may all be free from disease; may all see auspicious things; may no one be a partaker of sorrow. (b) भवन्तु = 'may (they) be' (लोट्, 3rd person plural); सन्तु = 'may (they) be' (लोट् of अस्); पश्यन्तु = 'may (they) see'; (also मा ... भवेत् = 'may (he) not be', विधिलिङ् with मा). (c) The prayer voices the universal goodwill — concern for सर्वे, all beings — out of which self-sacrifice for others naturally grows, as in Dadhichi.
questions.explanation: Translation, the blessing-forms, and the link to atmotsarga.
